name: Bonanjo
tagline: The administrative quarter by the river
description: The colonial-era administrative district beside the Wouri, with the ministries, the Pagode, the courts and the port authority, plus the Doual'art contemporary arts centre. It is the most orderly part of the city and where official business happens.
bestFor: Anyone dealing with government, the port or the banks
pros: More orderly than the rest of the city

name: Akwa
tagline: The commercial centre and the nightlife
description: The main commercial district, dense with shops, hotels, banks and the bars and clubs that make Douala's nightlife what it is. Boulevard de la Liberté runs through it and the whole area is busy at almost every hour.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the shops and nightlife on the doorstep
cons: Congested and noisy day and night

name: Bonapriso
tagline: The residential quarter the expatriates use
description: The most comfortable residential district, south of Akwa, with larger houses, embassies, international schools, good restaurants and supermarkets. It is where the oil, shipping and diplomatic communities live and where prices reflect it.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting security and services
cons: The most expensive area in the city
Insulated from the rest of Douala

name: Deido and New Bell
description: The large, dense residential districts north and east of the centre where most of Douala's population lives, with their own markets, maquis grill bars and a strong local identity. New Bell holds the central prison and the main market.
bestFor: Very long stays at genuinely local prices with French
pros: The best street food and maquis culture
cons: Requires real caution and local knowledge
No English and no visitor infrastructure

name: Kribi (beach town, 125 km south)
tagline: The beach town three hours south
description: A coastal town on the Atlantic south of Douala with sandy beaches, a deep-water port and the Lobé Falls, where a river drops directly into the sea, which is a rare thing anywhere. It is the escape most Douala residents take.
bestFor: Anyone who needs to get out of Douala's heat and congestion
pros: The Lobé Falls dropping into the sea
Cooler and far calmer than Douala
cons: A separate trip rather than a commute
